headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors because ACI can feed CRM/email data into Claude Code’s writable filesystem and broad network/tool access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ACI can surface CRM/email/research content through MCP or direct function calls, and Claude Code can read files and use MCP. If ACI output is copied into files or prompts, Claude Code may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The shared bridge is plausible, but not proven by docs alone, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF ACI output is written into a file or pasted into Claude Code prompts
IF Claude Code is configured to ingest MCP/file content as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a prompt-injection warning banner to ACI outputs
Require Claude Code to treat ACI text as untrusted data
Use a separate staging file for ACI output
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ACI touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data, while Claude Code reads repo files/user directories and has broad network egress. If sensitive ACI data is placed in shared files or prompts, Claude Code can transmit it to api.anthropic.com or other configured endpoints. That creates a realistic exfiltration path in default use, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF ACI data is stored in a shared workspace or pasted into Claude Code
IF Claude Code sends context containing those files to its backend or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep CRM/email data out of shared directories

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write files and modify git state, and ACI supports multiple instances with direct function calls/MCP. Both can operate on shared filesystem-backed state, so concurrent edits can clobber files or git history. Because the profiles explicitly show overlapping mutable surfaces and no locking, high conflict risk is justified.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same working tree or shared directory
IF both agents modify the same files or git branch without external locking
mitigations: Pause one agent during git operations
Check git status before each write

D_cascading_error.rationale: ACI can generate CRM/email/calendar actions or research outputs, and Claude Code can consume files and act through shell, git, or MCP. If Claude Code treats ACI output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into code changes or external actions. The pathway exists, but the profiles do not show fully automatic downstream execution, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Claude Code uses ACI-produced text as the sole source for edits or commands
IF ACI output is not independently verified before action
mitigations: Cross-check ACI outputs against source data
Limit Claude Code to draft-only mode

E_compliance.rationale: ACI handles CRM, email, calendar, and support data, while Claude Code runs locally but can send context to Anthropic and configured MCP servers. If regulated or personal data from ACI is placed into Claude Code context, residency/retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from ACI is entered into Claude Code context
IF the configured Claude Code backend or MCP server retention differs from ACI policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in prompts
Confirm retention settings for MCP servers
requires-engineering: document a shared data-handling policy
